issues.body: `_fix_chain_model_pin` claims to return a pin only when `ladder[ladder.index(pin):]` is exactly the dispatcher intersection, but it compares the two with `set(...)`. In the live OpenAI tables, `fix_chain == ["sol", "luna"]` while `ESCALATION_LADDERS["openai"] == ["luna", "sol"]`. The helper therefore returns `"luna"`, and review-fix.yml expands that pin to `["luna", "sol"]`: the same members but the opposite preference order from the chain used by `allocator.claim`. This violates the documented equal-derivation/adopt contract and can change which tier is preferred if the workflow ever consumes the expanded chain independently. The self-tests exercise singleton, empty, unknown, and non-suffix intersections, but never assert the live full-chain expansion is order-identical, so they do not catch the defect.
issues.fix_hint: Validate ordered equality, e.g. compare `ladder[ladder.index(floor):] == fix_chain`, not set equality. Add a non-vacuous test for the live full OpenAI chain that asserts either exact ordered round-trip through `model_pin` or fail-closed refusal when the existing floor-only input cannot represent that order.
issues.title: Model-pin validation ignores chain order and accepts a different workflow chain

verdict.summary: The route intersection itself is fail-closed and the end-to-end tests cover the important singleton and empty-intersection cases. However, the model-pin representability check compares sets rather than ordered chains. For the live OpenAI full chain, this accepts a workflow expansion in the opposite order, contradicting the change's stated requirement that the dispatcher and workflow derive the same chain. Because routing chains encode preference order, this is a major soundness defect and the new tests leave that case uncovered.
